article.title: Raye, Rosalía and Ella Langley Lead Women-Dominated 2027 Grammys Field
article.summary: British singer Raye leads all nominees with 11 nods for the 69th annual Grammy Awards, heading a vibrant, women-dominated nominee class alongside Rosalía, Ella Langley, Olivia Rodrigo, and Phoebe Bridgers.

article.content_html:
Key Developments

The Recording Academy announced the nominations for the 69th annual Grammy Awards, showcasing a nominee class heavily dominated by acclaimed young women. British singer-songwriter Raye leads all contenders with an impressive 11 nods, powered by her jazz and R&B-throwback style and her album This Music May Contain Hope.

Spanish singer Rosalía secured nine nominations following the recent Latin Grammy success of her album Lux (Complete Works). Chart-dominating new country star Ella Langley, alongside collaborator Miranda Lambert, Olivia Rodrigo, and Phoebe Bridgers, secured seven nods apiece. Langley also made history as the first straight-up country artist to contend for the top album prize in eight years with her record Dandelion.

Other top contenders in the mix include Bruno Mars, R&B singer-songwriters Leon Thomas and Olivia Dean, Taylor Swift, Ariana Grande, and New York rock band Geese. The winners will be crowned on February 7 in Los Angeles, during a ceremony broadcast live on ABC and Disney+, marking a new media era for the Recording Academy.

Key Takeaways

  • Top Nominee: Raye leads the entire 2027 Grammy field with 11 nominations.
  • Country Milestone: Ella Langley becomes the first straight-up country artist in eight years to compete for album of the year.
  • Broadcasting Shift: The awards show will air live on ABC and Disney+, concluding a more than 50-year partnership with CBS.

Why It Matters

The 2027 Grammy lineup highlights a transformative shift toward a fresh generation of critical and commercial favorites, heavily anchored by innovative female artists across pop, country, R&B, and multilingual genres. Without the intense direct rivalry of past heavyweights like Swift, Beyoncé, or Adele, this year's competition celebrates broader artistic diversity and a rising vanguard of musical talent taking center stage.
